title: GPU drip throttle + dependency blackhole replay for multi-region SLO observability
creator: Ava Chen
description: Objective: Validate Redwood inference behavior when a single region experiences progressive GPU capacity degradation ("drip" throttling) combined with a silent downstream dependency failure (blackhole) to ensure SLOs, circuit breakers, and load-shedding behave predictably and fallbacks engage without systemic cascading failures. Scope: multi-region orchestration (primary region under test, at least one healthy failover region), serving runtime (batching + KV cache), routing policy validation, admission control, and on-path dependencies (metrics DB, auth proxy). We will run controlled replays that incrementally worsen GPU availability and then inject dependency blackholes at varying timings to exercise race conditions and burn-rate reporting. Deliverables: test harness configs, observability queries/dashboards, a postmortem template, and automated regression tests for the critical failure sequences.
steps: Prepare baseline: snapshot current SLOs and normal traffic profile using traffic-replay tool on perf cluster
Deploy controlled throttle: use chaos-agent to apply a 'drip' CPU/GPU throttling policy to a single region's GPU pool that reduces available compute by 10% every 5 minutes until 80% reduction
Simulate dependency blackhole: flip network proxy rule for metrics DB and auth proxy to blackhole mode (drop packets) for defined windows (30s, 2m, 10m) while throttle is at 30%, 60%, and 80%
Monitor routing and circuit breakers: validate circuit breaker opens per policy, check routing fallback to healthy region, and confirm admission control sheds load before latency SLO breach
Record telemetry: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, 4xx/5xx error rates, token-level cost, KV cache hit ratio, queue length, and SLO burn rate using provided dashboard panels
Run rollback and recovery: remove throttle and blackhole rules, validate that warm-up (KV cache, batching) returns to baseline and no long-term state corruption occurred
Postmortem and recommendations: collect logs, flamegraphs, and traces; produce a runbook update with automated mitigations and follow-up tickets
acceptance_criteria: Circuit breakers open within configured thresholds and prevent >5% of in-flight requests from contributing to SLO burn during severe degradation
Fallback routing directs at least 95% of eligible requests to healthy region within 30s of primary region electing to degrade
Admission control triggers load-shedding policies before p99 latency crosses SLO target for more than 2 consecutive minutes
No latent request duplication across regions (single-delivery semantics maintained)
Dashboards capture clear, reproducible signals for SLO burn-rate, and a summary alert template is produced for oncall use

notes: Trade-offs: aggressive throttling gives clearer failure modes but increases risk of collateral impact—we limited canary to 5% and enforce automated rollback triggers
Decision: prefer progressive 'drip' rather than immediate pool eviction to simulate real-world degradation (OOMs, preemption) and to surface slow-onset mitigations like cache warming failure
Follow-ups: add simulation for KV cache cold-start penalty as separate ticket; consider adding synthetic client retries to evaluate duplicate suppression
